summary.title: Add retry budgets and a dead-letter queue
summary.text: Jobs that fail now back off exponentially and stop after a bounded number of attempts. A job that runs out of attempts is buried in a new dead-letter table, and operators can list and requeue buried jobs through two new endpoints. A second acknowledgement of a job no longer marks it done twice, and Job.Err becomes Job.LastError.

area.text: The `queue` package runs taskline's background jobs: a `Worker` claims jobs from a `Store`, runs them and acknowledges or fails each one. The `api` package serves job lookups over HTTP from the same store.

reached_by.text: Every job passes through `Worker.Run`, so a failed run now reaches the retry policy there. The dead-letter endpoints join the job lookup in `Handler.Routes`, behind `RequireOperator`.

contracts.text: `Store` is an interface other stores implement, so a new method and a new `Ack` error reach every implementation. `RoleFromRequest` decides who is an operator, and the new endpoints trust it as it is.

related.text: `MemoryStore` is the store the tests use; it gains `Reset` and the stricter `Ack` alongside the interface.

review_exchange.summary: Two automated reviewers and a maintainer reviewed earlier heads. The first automated review's overflow note and the maintainer's request for an operator check were resolved by later commits, and a second automated finding about Requeue was resolved too. The final automated review approved the last commit but left one open must-fix thread: the operator role is read from a request header the client can set.

blocks.text: A job that fails should wait longer after each failure and stop after a bounded number of attempts, instead of retrying forever at a fixed delay.

steps.text: The delay after a failed attempt starts at Base, doubles with each further attempt and never exceeds Max
A job is exhausted once its attempt count reaches Budget
Jitter adds up to the configured fraction of the delay, so the delay never shrinks below the computed value
After a failure the worker sleeps for the policy's delay for the job's attempt count

blocks.text: A job that has used its whole retry budget should not be retried again or silently dropped; an operator should be able to see it and put it back.

steps.text: A job whose handler fails with no attempts left is recorded as a dead letter and takes no further retries
Requeue marks the entry requeued and resets the job to pending with zero attempts and no error
The migration adds the dead_letters table keyed by job id and a buried flag on jobs defaulting to false

items.text: Keep dead letters in their own table instead of a state on the jobs row, so the queue's claim query is unchanged
Bury only on failure, never after a successful last attempt

reasons.text: A new table and a jobs column ship in one migration that has no down step.
Requeue holds the dead-letter lock while calling Store.Reset, which takes the store lock.

risks.text: ON DELETE CASCADE removes a dead-letter row when its job is deleted, so pruning old jobs also erases their failure history
Requeue acquires the dead-letter lock and then the store lock, while Bury takes them in the same order only through Store.Fail; a future caller reversing the order could deadlock
Requeue did not check that the job was still buried before resetting it, so a second call could reset a job that had already started running
The buried_at index is descending and only serves the list endpoint; it adds write cost to every burial

data.bug: Two workers acknowledging the same job both succeeded, so a job that had since been requeued could be marked done by a stale acknowledgement.
data.fix: Ack checks that the job is running and otherwise returns ErrNotRunning, which the worker treats as already handled.

summary.text: Fixes a race where two workers acknowledging the same job both marked it done: Ack now fails with ErrNotRunning unless the job is running, and the worker treats that error as already handled.

evidence.claim: A second Ack of a done job returns ErrNotRunning and leaves the job done

The worker ignores ErrNotRunning from Ack and records any other Ack error as a failure

Consider returning 400 when limit is above the cap instead of clamping it.

Bury jobs that run out of attempts in a dead-letter table so an operator can look at them.
Add endpoints to list and requeue dead letters, and limit them to operators.
A second ack of the same job should not mark it done twice; fix it and rename Err to LastError.
Document the retry budget and dead letters, and bump golang.org/x/time while you are in go.mod.
